results.name: hs_resolve_identifier_as_function_or_script
results.evidence: Indexes the 0x14-byte syntax-node table (DAT_0087a474) for a node and its specifier child; calls hs_find_function_by_name and, on failure, FUN_004833a0 against a name in the string heap (DAT_006b14c0), caching the resolved index and setting a 'resolved as script' flag bit consumed later by hs_parse_nonprimitive.
results.summary: Resolves an unparsed identifier syntax-node to either a builtin function index or a user-script index, caching the result on the node.

results.name: hs_parse_nonprimitive
results.evidence: Strings 'global'/'script'/'i expected "script" or "global".' plus calls to hs_add_global/hs_add_script match the name exactly; code implements identifier resolution, type-compatibility checks (FUN_0048ac90) and 'global'/'script' keyword parsing.
results.summary: Parses a non-primitive expression token, resolving it as a global, script, function call, or variable reference and reporting the matching HS syntax errors.

results.name: hs_parse_real
results.evidence: String 'this is not a valid real number.' plus digit/'.'-scanning loop and a call to _atof storing the result as a float on the syntax node.
results.summary: Validates and parses a floating point literal token from the script source text into the node's real value field.

results.name: hs_parse_enum_value
results.evidence: Linearly scans a table (count at DAT_00746f8c+0x4b4, entries at +0x4b8, stride 0x28, name pointer at +0x1c) for an exact match of the token text, then checks the matched entry's category field against a per-return-type table (DAT_006574e4) before storing the entry's value on the node.
results.summary: Looks up a parsed enum/keyword token by exact name in a scenario reference table and stores its numeric value if the category matches the expected type.

results.name: hs_report_expected_enum_values
results.evidence: String '%s must be ' plus __stricmp scan of a per-type name table (PTR_LAB_0065b538/0065b53c indexed by return-type) and manual construction of a comma-separated, quoted list of valid names into the shared error buffer (DAT_006b14d8/dc).
results.summary: Builds the '<type> must be "a", "b" or "c"' compiler error message when a keyword/enum token fails to match any valid name for its expected type.

results.name: hs_parse_scenario_datum
results.evidence: String 'this is not a valid %s name' plus a generic {count,array}-pair scan using __stricmp with a caller-supplied element stride (param_1), matching the name-lookup pattern used by scenario tag-block name parsers.
results.summary: Generic parser that resolves a quoted name token against an arbitrary-stride scenario tag-block array by exact case-insensitive string match, storing the found index or reporting an error.

results.name: hs_parse_scenario_reference
results.evidence: Trivial thunk that calls hs_parse_scenario_datum(0x60); the fixed 0x60-byte stride identifies a specific (unidentified) scenario name-bearing tag block, so the inherited name 'hs_compile_and_evaluate' is not supported by the code shown.
results.summary: Thin wrapper around hs_parse_scenario_datum specialized for a 0x60-byte-stride scenario reference table whose exact tag block could not be identified.

results.name: hs_parse_object_name
results.evidence: Strings 'this is not a valid object name.' and 'this is not an object of type %s.'; looks up the name via FUN_0053ebb0 against the object_names block (DAT_00746f8c+0x208, stride 0x24, matching hs_parse_scenario_datum's family) and checks the object's type bit against the expected-type mask (DAT_006574e2).
results.summary: Parses an object-name token, resolves it to a scenario object_names index, and verifies the referenced object matches the expected HS object type.

results.name: hs_string_table_find_index
results.evidence: Generic byte-wise string comparison loop against an array of char* (param_2, count param_1) using an implicit search key in the in_EAX register; returns the matching index or -1.
results.summary: Linearly searches an array of C strings for an exact case-sensitive match and returns its index, or -1 if not found.

results.name: hs_object_datum_reference_list_build
results.evidence: Walks a 0x200-byte-stride datum array (DAT_0087a480) via FUN_004d0630's iterator convention, and for every entry whose 0x34 field is valid, creates a chained 0xc-byte reference-list node (datum_new into DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468) copying that field.
results.summary: Builds a linked reference list collecting a per-entry index field from every valid slot of an object-related datum array.

results.name: hs_object_datum_table_reset_all
results.evidence: Iterates the same 0x200-byte datum array (DAT_0087a480) via the 'iter'-XOR iterator convention and, for entries passing a predicate (FUN_0053f020==0), calls FUN_00487f50(entry,1,1), the object detach/place routine.
results.summary: Iterates all entries of an object-related datum array and resets/detaches each one whose predicate check fails.

results.name: hs_reference_list_test_predicate
results.evidence: Walks the DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468 chained reference list calling FUN_0053f020 per node, returning early with 0 or 1 depending on the char param_2 flag, implementing an AND-vs-OR short-circuit reduction over the list.
results.summary: Evaluates a boolean predicate across every object in a reference list, short-circuiting as either an 'all' or an 'any' test selected by a flag.

results.name: hs_object_test_angle_condition
results.evidence: Guards on FUN_004f6ec0(3) (a camera/context lookup) then converts param_2 from degrees to radians (x*0.017453292) before delegating to FUN_0056c100, matching the per-object predicate callback used by FUN_004879b0/FUN_00487ad0.
results.summary: Per-object predicate helper that converts an angle argument from degrees to radians and forwards it to a lower-level geometry test, gated by a context validity check.

results.name: hs_reference_list_any_matches_angle
results.evidence: Walks the DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468 reference list, filters entries by an object-type bitmask (mask 3) and a nonzero field, and calls FUN_004878f0(object,angle) per candidate, returning true on the first success.
results.summary: Returns true if any filtered object in a reference list satisfies the angle-based predicate implemented by FUN_004878f0.

results.name: hs_reference_list_any_matches_angle_filtered
results.evidence: Same reference-list walk and object-type mask as FUN_004879b0 but calls FUN_0056c100 directly with a degrees-to-radians converted angle and an extra unaff_BX gate flag.
results.summary: Variant of the reference-list angle test that adds an extra caller-supplied gating flag before invoking the geometry predicate.

results.name: hs_object_hierarchy_matches_type_mask
results.evidence: Recurses over an object's attachment chain (fields at 0x114/0x118/0x11c off the pointer stored in the 0xc-entry object table DAT_008603b0) calling FUN_00474db0, then falls back to checking a type-bitmask (0x1c) at +0xb4 combined with a flag bit at +500.
results.summary: Recursively checks whether an object or any of its attached child objects matches a small object-type bitmask or a specific flag.

results.name: hs_object_slot_validate_or_reset
results.evidence: Bounds-checks param_1 against a 0x200-entry table (DAT_006b8cb8); if the slot holds a valid object and FUN_00487c10 fails, calls FUN_004f5bd0, otherwise falls through to FUN_004f7370.
results.summary: Validates a cached object-slot reference against a type-mask test, resetting it via a fallback path when invalid or absent.

results.name: hs_object_datum_table_cleanup
results.evidence: First loop follows each object's 0x11c child-chain to its terminal element and calls FUN_0056c640(obj,0,1,1) (an object-delete-shaped call) when it differs from the head; second loop uses the data_iterator_next/FUN_004f6f20 'iter'-XOR cookie pattern over DAT_0087a480 to delete stray created objects by type via FUN_004f5aa0/FUN_004f59d0.
results.summary: Cleans up an object-related datum table at HS runtime reset, deleting orphaned children and dynamically created objects left over from the previous state.

results.name: hs_object_names_for_each
results.evidence: Iterates the scenario object_names block (count at DAT_00746f8c+0x204, array at +0x208, stride 0x24) - the same block hs_parse_object_name resolves names against - and invokes the caller-supplied callback for every entry that passes predicate FUN_00625430.
results.summary: Enumerates every scenario object_names entry and invokes a callback for each one that satisfies a predicate check.

results.name: hs_object_detach_and_place_at_flag
results.evidence: When param_2 set and the object's parent-link field (index 0x47 in its pointer-table entry) is valid, unlinks it from the parent hierarchy using matrix4x3_inverse/matrix4x3_transform_normal/matrix4x3_multiply to convert into world space and clears the parent/attachment bookkeeping fields; afterwards computes a forward vector from a scenario location table entry's yaw/pitch (DAT_00746f8c+0x4e8, stride 0x5c) and calls FUN_004f51c0 to (re)apply position/facing.
results.summary: Detaches an object from its current parent object using full 3D-transform math, then repositions and reorients it based on a scenario location-table entry.

results.name: hs_reference_list_skip
results.evidence: Walks the DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468 chained reference list a fixed number of steps (register in_ECX) starting from the list head of object in_EAX, discarding intermediate values, matching an index-seek helper for the reference-list abstraction used throughout this file.
results.summary: Advances N nodes down a reference list starting at a given object's list head, used to seek to the Nth element.

results.name: hs_object_set_clamped_fraction
results.evidence: Clamps param_1 to [0,1] (treating negative as 0) and stores param_1 * *(float*)(obj+0xdc) into *(float*)(obj+0xe4), the classic 'current = fraction * max' setter pattern; exact field (health/shield) not confirmed from this fragment alone.
results.summary: Sets an object field to a fraction (0.0-1.0, clamped) of a corresponding maximum field, consistent with a health or shield percentage setter.

results.name: hs_object_resolve_named_reference
results.evidence: If the register-passed name string is non-empty, follows the object's tag through the tag_instances array (DAT_0087bc14, stride 0x20, data pointer at +0x14 - the standard Blam tag lookup pattern) to a nested sub-tag's 0x4c-byte-stride named entry list (count at +0xc4, array at +0xc8) and __stricmp-matches the name, then forwards the resolved index to FUN_004f6c60.
results.summary: Resolves a name string to an index within a named sub-list of an object's tag data (e.g. a seat, region, or marker list) and passes the result to a setter.

results.name: hs_reference_list_apply
results.evidence: Walks the DAT_0087a464/DAT_0087a468 chained reference list end to end, calling FUN_004f7b00(value) for every referenced entry.
results.summary: Applies a callback to every object referenced by a reference list.

results.name: hs_objects_delete_by_type
results.evidence: Iterates the objects datum array via FUN_004f6f20 using the same 'iter'-XOR iterator cookie convention, matches each object's type field against unaff_ESI, deletes matches via FUN_004f5aa0/FUN_004f59d0, and finishes by calling the already-named objects_garbage_collection and block_list_compact.
results.summary: Deletes every live object of a given object type, then runs garbage collection and compacts the block list.

results.name: hs_effect_new_at_flag
results.evidence: Computes a forward vector from cos/sin of a scenario location entry's yaw/pitch fields (DAT_00746f8c+0x4e8, stride 0x5c, offsets 0x30/0x34) and passes it with the entry's position (+0x24) to FUN_00450980 alongside a fixed effect-table pointer (PTR_DAT_00696714), matching an effect-spawn call signature.
results.summary: Spawns a visual effect positioned and oriented at a scenario location (flag/camera point) table entry.

results.name: hs_effect_new_on_object_marker
results.evidence: Guards on two register-passed object/marker handles being valid and a state check via FUN_004f6080, then calls FUN_00450870 with position/orientation buffers and a fixed-scale trailing argument list matching the effect-spawn signature used by FUN_00488870.
results.summary: Spawns a visual effect attached to an object's marker, gated on the object and marker both being valid.

results.name: hs_sound_impulse_at_flag
results.evidence: Builds a fixed-size request structure from a scenario location entry's position (DAT_00746f8c+0x4e8, stride 0x5c, offset 0x24), resolves a sound id via FUN_005013a0/DAT_00746f9c's stride-0x10 table, and passes the structure to FUN_004edd30 with no attached object (-1).
results.summary: Plays a positional sound impulse at a scenario location's coordinates, not attached to any object.

results.name: hs_object_apply_damage_effect
results.evidence: Builds the identical fixed-size request structure as FUN_00488960 (position/sound-id fields) but sources the position via FUN_004f6900 and finishes by calling the already-named chimera__apply_damage on it, gated on a valid unaff_EBX object handle.
results.summary: Applies a damage effect (with an embedded sound) to an object using the same request structure shape as the flag sound-impulse helper.

results.name: hs_sound_get_gain_reference
results.evidence: String "the sound '%s' does not exist" plus two tag_lookup calls into the tag_instances array (DAT_0087bc14, stride 0x20, data pointer at +0x14), first returning a direct gain-modifier field, then falling back to a sound_looping-style tag's detail-sound gain field.
results.summary: Looks up a sound or sound_looping tag by name and returns a pointer to its gain-modifier value, reporting an error if neither tag exists.

results.name: hs_evaluate_random
results.evidence: Uses the Borland/Numerical-Recipes LCG constants (0x19660d, 0x3c6ef35f) to advance a PRNG state (DAT_00719cd0), maintains a bitset sized to the argument count to avoid re-picking the same branch, and drives the evaluation via the shared hs_evaluate_next_argument/hs_coerce_evaluated_result pair (FUN_0048a560/FUN_0048a640).
results.summary: Implements the HS 'random' special form: randomly selects and evaluates one not-yet-chosen child expression per invocation, avoiding repeats until the set is exhausted.

results.name: hs_evaluate_boolean_and_or
results.evidence: Seeds the running boolean result to true only when the opcode selector param_1 equals 5, then on each subsequent call combines the new evaluated boolean with the running result using AND semantics when param_1==5 and OR semantics otherwise - the classic short-circuit boolean reduce pattern.
results.summary: Per-call reducer implementing the HS 'and'/'or' special forms, short-circuiting the boolean combination based on the selected opcode.

results.name: hs_evaluate_arithmetic_reduce
results.evidence: Switch on the opcode selector param_1 implements +=(7), -=(8), *=(9), /=(10), min(11) and max(12) against a running float accumulator, matching the built-in arithmetic script functions '+','-','*','/','min','max'.
results.summary: Per-call reducer implementing the HS numeric '+','-','*','/','min' and 'max' special forms over a variadic argument list.

results.name: hs_evaluate_sleep
results.evidence: Initializes a default duration of 0x1e (30 ticks, i.e. one second at Halo's 30 Hz tick rate) and a start-tick snapshot from DAT_006f1d6c+0xc (current game tick), then on completion stores start_tick+duration (clamped to an optional end bound) into the thread frame's deferred-time field.
results.summary: Implements the HS 'sleep'/'sleep_until' special form, computing the game tick at which the calling thread should resume.

results.name: hs_evaluate_argument_list_fixed32
results.evidence: Reserves a fixed 32-element (0x80 byte) undefined4 array plus a count field on the thread frame; each reentrant call appends one evaluated value into the array (capped at 0x20 entries) until the reference-list link is exhausted.
results.summary: Collects up to 32 evaluated argument values into a fixed-size array, one value per reentrant call, for a variadic HS operation.

results.name: hs_runtime_initialize
results.evidence: Strings 'hs thread' and 'hs globals' passed to FUN_005380d0 (a datum-array allocator) plus data_delete_all() and a loop of 0x1eb datum_new_at_index_with_salt calls reserving the fixed low-index globals range.
results.summary: Allocates the HS thread and globals datum arrays and reserves the first 0x1eb global slots at engine start-up.

results.name: hs_scenario_scripts_initialize
results.evidence: Clears runtime state and calls data_delete_all(), creates a root thread datum, then for every scenario global (DAT_00746f8c+0x4a8/0x4ac) allocates its runtime slot and evaluates its default-value expression, writing the result back via the global-write dispatcher (FUN_0048b030); a second loop over the scripts block (+0x49c/+0x4a0) auto-starts every script whose type is not 3 or 4 (static/stub), matching HS's startup/dormant/continuous auto-run rule.
results.summary: Resets the HS runtime for a newly loaded scenario: reinitializes global variables to their default values and auto-starts all non-static, non-stub scripts.

results.name: hs_globals_delete_temporary
results.evidence: Clears the hs-thread-array active flag then calls datum_delete for every globals-array slot at or beyond index 0x1eb, the same reserved-slot boundary established by hs_runtime_initialize.
results.summary: Deletes every dynamically allocated HS global beyond the fixed reserved range, used when tearing down the HS runtime.

results.name: hs_runtime_update
results.evidence: Iterates all active HS threads (FUN_004d0630) and, for each whose scheduled-time field is at or before the current game tick (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc), steps it via FUN_0048a370; tracks whether any thread is an immediate-evaluation thread and conditionally triggers a recompile/reload path (FUN_00483310).
results.summary: Per-tick HS scheduler: advances every thread whose deadline has arrived and triggers a reload check when nothing else is pending.

results.name: hs_evaluate_expression_immediate
results.evidence: Only runs while DAT_006b15e8 (scripts-enabled flag) is set; allocates a type-2 thread via FUN_0048a2f0(2) for the given node, drives it once with hs_evaluate_next_argument (FUN_0048a560), and either finalizes/deletes it (FUN_0048a370) if flagged complete or returns its stored result field.
results.summary: Synchronously compiles and evaluates a single HS expression node to completion, returning its result value or failure.

results.name: hs_call_script_by_name
results.evidence: Combines hs_thread_find_by_script_name (FUN_0048a9f0) with hs_thread_restart (FUN_0048a790), matching HS's ability to invoke a named user script as if it were a function call.
results.summary: Finds a script's existing thread by name and restarts it, implementing calling a named HS script like a function.

results.name: hs_thread_new
results.evidence: Calls datum_new on the thread array, clears the scratch-list head/cursor fields, stores the target node index (in_EAX) and type (param_1), and initializes the deferred-time field to a 'not scheduled' sentinel (-2) for 'static'-typed scripts based on the scripts table's return-type field.
results.summary: Allocates and initializes a new HS thread datum for evaluating a given syntax node.

results.name: hs_thread_evaluate_node
results.evidence: Drives the thread's current node through hs_evaluate_next_argument (FUN_0048a560) in a loop while its scratch-cursor list is non-empty and the game tick budget (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc) has not been exceeded, then on completion either yields the result to its parent's global slot or deletes the thread datum if it is a type-2 (immediate) thread.
results.summary: Steps an HS thread's evaluation of its current syntax node, resuming later if the per-tick time budget runs out, and finalizes it on completion.

results.name: hs_evaluate_next_argument
results.evidence: Reads the syntax-node flags byte and either pushes a new scratch-list frame for the node's child (allocating and linking a new list entry) or, when a 'resolved constant/global' flag is set, calls hs_global_get_value_pointer (FUN_0048a720) and hs_coerce_global_value (FUN_0048ad10) to fetch a ready value directly.
results.summary: Schedules the next child expression of a syntax node for evaluation, or short-circuits by fetching an already-resolved constant or global's value.

results.name: hs_coerce_evaluated_result
results.evidence: Compares the just-evaluated child's declared type against the parent's expected return type and, if they differ and neither is the wildcard type 3, calls a coercion function via the large per-type-pair dispatch table DAT_0068bc10 (or FUN_004f73c0 for the boolean-ish type range), then stores the result into the parent's argument slot.
results.summary: Coerces an evaluated child expression's result to the type expected by its parent node using a per-type-pair conversion dispatch table.

results.name: hs_global_get_value_pointer
results.evidence: Splits the register-passed reference on its high bit to index either the low or high half of the HS globals datum array (DAT_0087a46c, stride 8) and returns the stored value pointer field at offset 4.
results.summary: Returns the storage pointer for an HS global variable given its packed reference/index.

results.name: hs_thread_frame_advance
results.evidence: Dereferences the thread frame's scratch-list cursor pointer (offset 0x10) through itself, advancing to the next linked scratch chunk - the pop/advance half of the reference-list-node allocator used elsewhere in this file.
results.summary: Advances an HS thread frame's scratch-list cursor to the next linked chunk.

results.name: hs_thread_restart
results.evidence: If the thread's scratch cursor is active it is reset to zero, restoring a saved resume value from offset 0xc when the 'has saved continuation' flag (bit 1 of the flags byte) is set; otherwise it checks the first child's resolved type against 0x14 (a 'script'/block node type) to decide whether to restart from the beginning via hs_thread_frame_advance.
results.summary: Restarts or resumes an existing (dormant) HS thread, either continuing from its saved state or beginning evaluation over.

results.name: hs_evaluate_typed_arguments
results.evidence: Reserves a param_2-sized int array plus a count field on the thread frame; on init evaluates the reference-list head, and while the running count is below param_2 and the just-evaluated value's type matches the expected-type array (param_3), evaluates the next argument via hs_evaluate_next_argument, otherwise returns the fully-typed argument buffer.
results.summary: Evaluates a fixed-arity, statically typed argument list one argument per call, validating each against an expected-type array before returning the completed buffer.

results.name: hs_thread_find_by_script_index
results.evidence: Iterates active HS threads (FUN_004d0630) comparing each thread frame's script-index field (offset 4) against the given short param_1, returning the matching thread handle.
results.summary: Finds the currently active or dormant HS thread associated with a given script index.

results.name: hs_thread_find_by_script_name
results.evidence: Iterates active HS threads (FUN_004d0630), and for each with a valid script-index field, __stricmp-compares the inline name embedded in the scenario scripts table entry (DAT_00746f8c+0x4a0, stride 0x5c) against param_1, returning the matching thread handle.
results.summary: Finds the currently active or dormant HS thread whose associated script matches the given name.

results.name: hs_string_is_single_char
results.evidence: Computes the string length via a scan-to-nul loop and returns true only when (length-1)==0, i.e. the string is exactly one character long.
results.summary: Returns whether a C string consists of exactly one character.

results.name: hs_object_orient
results.evidence: Nine-byte thunk that tail-calls FUN_006391b4 with no explicit arguments visible in the decompilation, implying register-passthrough; the pre-existing non-FUN_ name is plausible for an HS builtin but unverifiable from this fragment alone.
results.summary: Thin forwarding wrapper to an object-orientation routine, consistent with an HS built-in function implementation.

results.name: hs_reference_list_append_new
results.evidence: Guards on param_1 != -1, allocates a new 0xc-byte reference-list datum via datum_new (clearing its flags/next fields), and calls FUN_0048b2a0(param_1) to link it in.
results.summary: Allocates and appends a new reference-list node for a given object index, if valid.

results.name: hs_type_mask_is_subset
results.evidence: Looks up two type bitmasks in table DAT_00657538 indexed by in_AX and in_CX and returns true only when in_CX's mask fully contains in_AX's bits, implementing a polymorphic-type membership test.
results.summary: Tests whether one HS type's bitmask is fully contained within another's, used for polymorphic type compatibility (e.g. 'object' encompassing 'unit'/'vehicle').

results.name: hs_types_are_compatible
results.evidence: Returns true immediately for an exact match or the wildcard type 3, otherwise consults the same per-type-pair dispatch presence table (DAT_0068bc10) used by hs_coerce_evaluated_result, with hs_type_mask_is_subset (FUN_0048ac60) handling the polymorphic type ranges; called by hs_parse_nonprimitive to produce its 'i expected a %s, but this function/script returns a %s.' compile errors.
results.summary: Compile-time check for whether a value of one HS type can be used where another HS type is expected.

results.name: hs_coerce_global_value
results.evidence: Mirrors hs_coerce_evaluated_result's per-type-pair dispatch (DAT_0068bc10) and boolean-range special case (FUN_004f73c0), but operates on a plain register-passed value/type pair rather than an evaluated node result; used from hs_evaluate_next_argument's short-circuit global-fetch path.
results.summary: Coerces a raw HS global's value to a requested type using the shared per-type-pair conversion dispatch table.

results.name: hs_evaluate_variadic_arguments
results.evidence: Reserves a 32-element (0x80 byte) undefined4 array plus a count field on the thread frame, appends one caller-supplied value per call, and once the reference-list is exhausted or 32 entries are reached, writes the count and array pointer out through param_3/param_4 and returns success; used by 13 call sites, far more than the fixed-arity typed variant.
results.summary: Generic variadic argument collector used pervasively for evaluating HS script/function calls, accumulating up to 32 values before returning the completed list.

results.name: hs_global_read_value
results.evidence: Switches on a per-global type code (5 through 0x2b) stored in a descriptor table (PTR_PTR_0068b398) to read the underlying live game variable through a typed pointer into the HS global's own storage at offset 4, matching the get half of a globals variable get/set dispatcher.
results.summary: Copies the current value of a bound engine global variable into its corresponding HS global's storage, dispatched by type.

results.name: hs_global_write_value
results.evidence: Mirrors hs_global_read_value's type-code switch over the same descriptor table (PTR_PTR_0068b398) but writes the HS global's stored value back through the typed pointer into the underlying engine variable.
results.summary: Writes an HS global's current value back into its bound underlying engine variable, dispatched by type.
